name: Rechargeable lithium vanadium
plain: A rechargeable 3-volt coin battery, sold with the VL prefix, for memory and clock backup and keyless entry. It holds less than an ML battery of the same size and needs a charger set to its own voltage.
summary: Rechargeable lithium vanadium coin batteries, sold with the VL prefix, pair a lithium alloy anode with a vanadium pentoxide cathode for 3.0V nominal. They are charged at a constant 3.4V and used for memory and clock backup, keyless entry and other low-drain devices.
body:
## How it works

Panasonic's VL series uses vanadium oxide as the positive electrode, a lithium alloy as the negative electrode, and a non-aqueous solvent as the electrolyte. Panasonic decodes its naming as V for vanadium pentoxide lithium battery and L for round, followed by the diameter in millimeters and the height in tenths of a millimeter: the VL2020 is 20mm in diameter and 2.0mm high. Wikipedia lists the Li/Al and vanadium pentoxide VL battery as a rechargeable lithium metal system at 3V with a lithium-aluminum alloy anode.

## Discharge behavior

Nominal voltage is 3.0V. Panasonic rates the VL2020 at 20.0mAh to a 2.5V cutoff at 20°C, with a continuous drain of 0.07mA, and lists retention of high discharge voltage as a feature of the series. The operating range is −20 to 60°C, self-discharge is 2% per year at 20°C, and cycle life is about 1,000 cycles at 10% depth of discharge relative to nominal capacity.

Charging is constant-voltage, with a guaranteed charging voltage of 3.4 ± 0.15V (3.25 to 3.55V) from −20 to 60°C. As with the ML series, Panasonic warns that trickle charging of the kind used for nickel-cadmium batteries must never be used, because the battery voltage rises to about 5V and performance deteriorates. A charge voltage above the specification raises internal resistance; around 4V the positive terminal, which is the case, can corrode and leak. Below the specification, capacity does not fully recover.

## Uses

Memory backup, RTC backup in printers, multifunction machines, medical and factory automation equipment, remote keyless entry and fire alarms, according to Panasonic's VL2020 datasheet. Panasonic Industry Europe also lists tracking and RFID, IoT systems and remote controls.

## History

Panasonic Industry Europe cites over 30 years of manufacturing experience with VL batteries.

## Status

Current. VL is a manufacturer prefix rather than an IEC designation.
strengths: About 1,000 cycles at 10% depth of discharge
limitations: Low capacity: 20.0mAh for the VL2020, against 45.0mAh for the ML2020
Very low current: 0.07mA continuous for the VL2020
Needs a constant-voltage charger set at 3.4 ± 0.15V
safety: Never trickle charge: voltage rises to about 5V (Panasonic)
A charge voltage near 4V can corrode the case and cause leakage
Coin format carries the button battery ingestion hazard
